newsitem.title: GERMANY: Rexrodt says Q1 growth in line with expectations.
newsitem.headline: Rexrodt says Q1 growth in line with expectations.

text.p: Economics Minister Guenter Rexrodt said that Germany's 1.4 percent year-on-year economic growth rate in the first quarter was in line with expectations.
Three fewer workdays in the quarter held growth back. Adjusted for this calendar effect, which will be reversed in the second quarter, the growth rate would have been 2.75 percent, he said.
Growth in gross domestic product (GDP) remained export-driven with domestic demand still slack, he said.

"First-quarter growth in gross domestic product (GDP) is in line with the expectations underlying the government's annual report on the economy," Rexrodt said. "Growth resumed, as expected, following a pause at the end of 1996," he said.

Rexrodt said vigorous exports showed that German competitiveness had improved due to lower unit-wage costs, the correction in the mark's value against the dollar, and healthy economies in other countries.
Private consumption in Germany was stagnant, and construction investment declined. Capital investment continued to grow, but lacked vigour, he said.
Conditions were better than in a long time for revived investment, which was needed to create new jobs and capacity for further growth, he said.
Rexrodt named several positive factors visible in the economy, such as rising business confidence and capacity utilisation, low interest rates, higher profits, moderate wages and stable prices.

"The economic upswing, which has remained moderate so far, has not yet had a positive effect on the labour market," he said. "A penetrating improvement can only be expected if investment grows more dynamic and domestic demand grows more strongly again."
